# What the machine data says of the disks behind its pools, in the lines .scripts/capture.sh writes: every serial number and world wide name here is
# made up, and the rest is as it was. It was rebuilt from listings of data's /dev and /sys taken by hand, before capture.sh could be run there, so
# two things are filled in as the kernel lays them out rather than read: each partition's number, and each slot's number, from the name its
# enclosure gives it. sda's page of names was read later, from the running machine.
#
# TrueNAS 25.10 in a virtual machine: the pool boot-pool on a virtual disk (sda) with no page of its serial number, known by the name its maker
# gives it in its page of names, and the pool host on another (sdbh) with one, neither with a world wide name to give; 56 SAS disks in the pool
# data behind two Broadcom 9500 cards and three enclosures, 2 more as its spares, and 2 NVMe disks as its cache.
